Author: @leigoi1328
Content:
Taiwan is NOT a country:

1. Historical Integration:
Taiwan has been part of China since the 17th century (since 1683 under Qing rule) or even as far back as Yuan Dynasty.

2. Republic of China (ROC):
Taiwan’s official name is the Republic of China (ROC).

3. ROC Constitution:
The ROC Constitution does not define Taiwan as separate; it claims sovereignty over all China including Taiwan, which echoes the PRC's One China Policy of mainland and Taiwan being one entity.

4. De Jure vs De Facto:
Taiwan has its government, currency, passport, and military, aka, it governs itself (de facto), but lacks legal ground (de jure) as a sovereign state.

5. UN Proposals Rejected (Two Chinas):
1960s UN proposals for both PRC and ROC as “Two Chinas” were overwhelmingly rejected.

6. UN Proposals Rejected (One China, One Taiwan):
1970s–80s UN proposals for “One China, One Taiwan” were also overwhelmingly rejected.

7. UN Resolution 2758 (One China):
In 1971, the UN recognized PRC as China’s sole legal government of all China, expelling the ROC and denying Taiwan separate status.

8. "PRC Never Controlled Taiwan" Argument:
PRC’s lack of control over Taiwan in practice (de facto) doesn’t grant Taiwan legal (de jure) sovereignty.

9. "Taiwan's Self Determination" Argument:
Taiwan’s status should not be decided by only its residents; it concerns all of China and requires consensus from both sides, including the mainland.

10. "Resolution 2758 never explicitly mentioned Taiwan" Argument:
The unity of China, including Taiwan, was universally understood as shown by the rejection of “Two Chinas” and “One China, One Taiwan” UN proposals. Explicitly naming Taiwan in Resolution 2758 would have been as unnecessary as listing other provinces of China.

11. Analogy:
Imagine someone(Taiwan) managing and living in a room of a large house(China), fully in control of that room(de facto), but without legal ownership(de jure) or recognition from the rest of the household(rest of China) and the neighbours(rest of the world) that it’s a separate property.

Content:
China definitely is taking notes on Ukraine, specifically on how the west “kind of helped” but not enough for Ukraine to repel the invasion in a quick manner, and in the end, Ukraine could be losing some of its land to become new Separatist states under Russia. Likewise, China, now knowing the west will try its best to help without actually helping, is going to swoop in and try to take a chunk, if not all, of Taiwan.

This is all similar stuff to what happened in the 1930’s. Italy, Japan, and Germany all started testing their new gear by bullying around a smaller nation (the USSR and US did this too, if you consider the Poland deal with Germany and the US’s Pacific Islands imperialism). 

We are living through the pre-war period right now. The world’s largest armies are testing their gear by bullying smaller nations, and sizing up their success to the success of other large nations’ incursions on smaller countries land. Call me crazy, but I think World War III started with the (second) invasion of Ukraine, and right now is simply the “phony war” period where everyone just sits on their asses to see who’s going to do what next. Similar to how people debate whether WWII started with the invasion of China in 1936 or if it started by the invasion of Poland in 1939, people in the future are going to debate on if WWIII started with the invasion of Ukraine in 2021 or the invasion of Taiwan in 2025/2026 (yes, I think it’ll be that soon.) 

I don’t think big players are going to start directly attacking each other yet, but when they do, I don’t think nukes are going to be used as people think. They’re going to be used on carrier strike groups in the deep ocean, because “it’ll have the least impact” (notice how I put quotations), as well as on heavily fortified, isolated bases such as the US’s pacific islands or China’s pacific islands as last resorts. They’re not going to be used on densely populated areas like Hiroshima or Nagasaki. That was a mistake from the past that won’t be made again. 

WWIII won’t be like WWII, with everybody ganging up on a clear evil like Hitler and his allies, nor will it be a nuclear holocaust. It’ll be more like WWI, with countries going to war solely for—well—the sake of going to war and to see who has the biggest stick. Likewise, it’s going to include a lot of stalemates like we’re seeing in Ukraine and Palestine, and as I can imagine, Taiwan too, with little gains and lots of loss of life—but still not as much as the loss of life compared to WWI. 

Regardless, it’ll be a war, which isn’t good for any of us. Let’s choose peace and delay the march to war while we can.
